---
title: "Listings"
description: "Generate lists of pages or hand-written entries with `listing:`."
---

## Contents

`contents:` names what a listing shows. Each entry is either a glob that
selects project documents, or an inline record — a small map that *is* an
item.

### Globs

A glob resolves against the file it is written in — the listing page's
own directory for front-matter patterns, the directory holding a
`_metadata.yml`, or the project root for patterns in `_quarto.yml`. `*`
matches one directory level; use `**/` or name a directory to search
subdirectories. A leading `/` anchors at the project root from anywhere.
See [`Q-12-19`](/errors/listing/Q-12-19.qmd) for the full rules and the
common ways a pattern matches nothing.

### Records

```yaml
listing:
  id: cards
  type: grid
  contents:
    - title: "Get started"
      description: "Download and install"
      image: images/rocket.png
    - title: "Release notes"
      path: https://example.com/releases
```

A record's `title`, `subtitle`, `description`, `author`, `date`,
`date-modified`, `image`, `image-alt`, `categories`, `order`, `path`,
`reading-time-minutes` and `word-count` (and other fields besides) are the
same fields a document supplies. Any other key becomes a custom field a
custom template can read as `$it.key$` (also `$it.extra.key$`) — which
also makes a misspelled field name easy to miss, since it's kept rather
than rejected; watch for [`Q-12-22`](/errors/listing/Q-12-22.qmd) if an
item is missing a field you thought you set. A record needs a `title:` or
a `path:` to render meaningfully — one with neither produces an
empty-titled item ([`Q-12-21`](/errors/listing/Q-12-21.qmd)). Relative
`image:` and `path:` values resolve against the file the listing is
written in.

### Titles and descriptions are markdown

An item's `title`, `subtitle` and `description` are markdown, whether
they come from a document's front matter or from a record. Their
formatting shows in the listing as it does on the page: a title such as
``Fix `_scope`: a *lexical* regression`` keeps its code span and its
emphasis. Links inside them are shown as plain text, since each item is
already a link, and footnotes are left out.

A listing shows each of them as a single paragraph. Write a
`description:` as one paragraph; one written as several (a YAML block
scalar with a blank line in it, or a list) is joined into one, with a
warning ([`Q-12-26`](/errors/listing/Q-12-26.qmd)).

### Where descriptions and images come from

For an item that is a project document, the listing uses the first
description it finds in this order:

1. `description:` under `listing-item:` in the document's front matter;
2. `description:`;
3. `abstract:`;
4. the first paragraph of the rendered page.

The image follows the same pattern: `image:` under `listing-item:`, then
`image:`, then the page's preview image. The preview image is an image
with the class `.preview-image`, or else one whose file name contains
`preview`, `feature`, `cover` or `thumbnail`, or else the first image on
the page.

A value you write is used as written; Quarto derives one from the page
only when you didn't. `listing-item:` is there for the case where the
listing should say something different from the page's own
`description:` or `image:`. A description longer than the listing's
`max-description-length` (default 175 characters; `0` turns the limit
off) is cut at a word boundary, whichever way it was chosen. Derived
descriptions appear in every layout, tables included.

The derived description is taken from the *rendered* page, so a page
whose text comes from running code still gets one. In the browser-based
editor, which does not do that last step, the derived description is the
page's first paragraph as written instead.

A record's own `description:` and `image:` are always used as written.
A record that points at a document but leaves them out gets the
document's, chosen as above.

### Records that point at a document

`path: guide/install.qmd` merges the record over that document's own
entry: the record's fields win, the document supplies the rest (link,
description, date, …). A `path:` that is an external URL or a
non-document file is used as the link as written. A `path:` that looks
like a document (has a `.qmd`/`.md`/`.Rmd`/`.ipynb` extension) but names
one the project doesn't render — a typo, or a file outside
`project.render` — builds the item from the record's own fields alone
and keeps the link as written, and warns
([`Q-12-20`](/errors/listing/Q-12-20.qmd)).

### Order

Items are sorted by the listing's `sort:`. **With no `sort:` key, the
default is `order asc, title asc`** — but that default applies only to a
listing that contains at least one *document*: an item matched by a
`contents:` glob, or a record whose `path:` names a document the project
renders.

A listing built entirely from records — the usual shape of a
hand-curated card list — gets no default sort, and its items appear in
the order you wrote them:

```yaml
listing:
  contents:
    - title: "Get started"     # renders first
    - title: "Explore features"
    - title: "Advanced usage"
```

Add one glob, or one record whose `path:` points at a page in the
project, and the default sort applies to the whole listing again —
alphabetizing the records along with it, since records carry no `order:`
of their own. To keep such a list in the order you wrote it, set
`sort: false`, or give each record an explicit `order:`.

With `sort: false`, items appear in the order of the `contents:` entries
— records included — with one exception: when `contents:` holds only
negated patterns (e.g. `["!draft.qmd", {title: Featured}]`), the implicit
"everything else" positive counts as declared before every entry, so a
record sorts after those items no matter where it's written. (Quarto 1
placed all records after all glob matches.)

### Fields

`fields:` lists which parts of each item a listing shows. In the `default`
and `grid` layouts it decides what each card draws:

```yaml
listing:
  type: grid
  fields: [date, title, description]
```

These cards show only a date, a title and a description. There is no
image area, and no author, subtitle, reading time or categories, even
for items that have them. Without `fields:`, a listing uses its type's
default set and keeps only the fields at least one item has, plus
`image`. An item that is a project document always counts as having a
description and an image, since Quarto can derive both from the
rendered page.

`image` is the exception: when it's in the set, every card gets an image
area. An item with no image of its own (see
[Where descriptions and images come from](#where-descriptions-and-images-come-from))
gets the listing's `image-placeholder:`, or an empty placeholder. If none of your items have images, leave `image`
out of `fields:` to avoid a row of empty boxes.

### Not yet supported

YAML files in `contents:` (Quarto 1's `contents: items.yml`) are skipped
with a warning ([`Q-12-23`](/errors/listing/Q-12-23.qmd)); move the
records inline.

## Pages and categories in the browser

A `default` or `grid` listing with more items than its `page-size:`
shows one page at a time, with page links below it. The default page
size is 25 for `default` listings, 18 for `grid` and 30 for `table`.

When `categories:` is on, clicking a category — in the sidebar list or
on an item — narrows the listing to the items in that category, and a
"No matching items" message stands in when nothing matches. The current
page and category are kept in the address (`#category=…`), so a
filtered view can be linked to.

The listing's element on the page has the id `listing-` followed by the
listing's `id:`. A page's only listing, when it sets no `id:`, is
`#listing-listing`.

Not yet supported:

- **`table` listings** paginate and filter in Quarto 1, but not yet in
  Quarto 2: every row is shown.
- **`sort-ui` and `filter-ui`** controls are not rendered yet.
- **`custom` listings** are left as your template wrote them, without
  paging or category filtering in the browser.
- **The live preview** — the default `q2 preview`, and Quarto Hub —
  shows every item on one page. `q2 render` and
  [`q2 preview --static`](preview.qmd) produce the interactive page.

## Custom templates

Beyond the built-in `default`, `grid` and `table` layouts, a listing can
render through a template you write:

```yaml
listing:
  id: cards
  type: custom
  template: card.template
  contents: "guides/*.qmd"
```

`template:` resolves relative to the page that declares the listing.
Quarto 2 custom listing templates are **doctemplates** — the
`$variable$` syntax Pandoc templates use — not the EJS templates of
Quarto 1. A doctemplate cannot run code; it interpolates values,
branches on them and loops over them. The output is markdown, parsed
back into the page, so raw HTML goes in a ```` ```{=html} ```` block just as
it would in a `.qmd` file.

That last point has a consequence worth knowing before you write a
template: paths inside raw HTML are **not** resolved. A link or image
written as raw HTML keeps the path you gave it, so links to project
documents ship unrewritten and images are never copied into the output
— with no warning either way. Write links and images as markdown. See
[Listing templates](listing-templates.qmd#links-and-images-must-be-markdown)
for the idiom, and [Paths in websites](paths.qmd#raw-html-is-not-rewritten)
for the same rule as it applies to page content.

### Syntax

| Directive | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `$listing.id$`, `$it.title$` | Interpolate a value; dotted paths walk into maps. |
| `${it.title}` | The same, brace-delimited — use it when the value is followed immediately by text that would otherwise run into the name. |
| `$for(items)$ … $endfor$` | Loop. Inside the body the current item is `$it$` (also `$items$`). Nested loops over a list-valued field work, and the inner `$it$` shadows the outer. |
| `$sep$` | Inside a loop: emitted between items, not after the last. |
| `$if(it.image)$ … $elseif(it.icon)$ … $else$ … $endif$` | Branch on truthiness (empty strings and missing keys are false). |
| `$it.title/uppercase$` | Apply a pipe. Available: `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `chomp`, `nowrap`, `alpha`, `roman`, `first`, `last`, `rest`, `allbutlast`, `length`, `pairs`, `reverse`, `left`, `center`, `right`. |
| `$it:item-default()$` | Apply a partial to a value — here the built-in `item-default` partial, or a same-named `.template` file next to your template file. |
| `$-- text` | Comment; not rendered. |
| `$$` | A literal dollar sign — on its own this is still literal text and does not make a file a template. |

A template that contains none of these is not a template: Quarto 2
warns ([`Q-12-24`](/errors/listing/Q-12-24.qmd)) and skips the listing
rather than paste the file into the page.

### Values a template can read

- **`listing.*`** — the listing's own configuration: `id`, `type`,
  `fields`, `field-links`, `table-header` (a pre-rendered markdown
  header row for the `table` layout), `sort-ui`, `filter-ui`,
  `page-size`, `grid-columns`, `template-params` (anything under
  `template-params:` in the YAML, passed through for your template's
  own options).
- **`items`** — one entry per item, each with `title`, `subtitle`,
  `description`, `author`, `authors`, `date`, `date-modified`, `image`,
  `image-alt`, `categories`, `path` (the link target, already
  page-relative), `filename`, `reading-time`, `reading-time-minutes`,
  `word-count`, `order`, plus `image-html`, `category-html` and
  `table-row` pre-rendered snippets. Custom fields from an inline record
  or from a document's `listing-item.extra` are readable directly
  (`$it.icon$`) and under `$it.extra.icon$`. `title`, `subtitle` and
  `description` are **markdown** on one line, already escaped: use them
  where the template writes markdown (`### [$it.title$]($it.path$)`).
  Inside a raw HTML block, where markdown would show as source, use
  their rendered twins `title-html`, `subtitle-html` and
  `description-html` instead.
- **`project.*`** — `site-url` and `title` from the website
  configuration.

Only `title` is guaranteed present on every item. `path` is present
whenever the item has a link target — a document, or a record with
`href:` — and absent for a record with neither. **The rest are absent
when the item lacks them, and reading an absent value warns** with
[`Q-12-10`](/errors/listing/Q-12-10.qmd) — so guard optional reads:
`$if(it.subtitle)$…$endif$`.

Four more per-item values exist for specific jobs:

- **`outputHref`** — the item's rendered output path. For feeds and
  cross-references, *not* for links: it is already resolved, so it
  bypasses the path rewriting that makes `path` work.
- **`description-placeholder-begin`** / **`-end`** and
  **`image-placeholder-begin`** / **`-end`** — envelope markers that let
  Quarto fill in a missing description or image after both documents
  render. See
  [Listing templates](listing-templates.qmd#descriptions-and-the-placeholder-envelope).
- **`show.<field>`** — true for each field in the listing's field set:
  its `fields:`, or the type's defaults (see [Fields](#fields)). A
  `type: custom` listing without `fields:` uses every field that at
  least one item has, as in Quarto 1.
- **`metadata-attrs`** — `data-index`, `data-categories` and
  `data-listing-<field>-sort` attributes, the equivalent of Quarto 1's
  `metadataAttrs()`. Emit it in attribute position — inside a div's
  braces (`::: {.item $it.metadata-attrs$}`) or on a tag in a
  ```` ```{=html} ```` block; interpolated as markdown text its quotes
  are curled into invalid HTML.

These are the most useful values; the built-in templates show the rest.

The built-in layouts are themselves doctemplates and make the best
reference: `listing-default.template`, `listing-grid.template`,
`listing-table.template` and the `item-default` partial live under
[`crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/templates/`](https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/tree/main/crates/quarto-core/src/project/listing/templates)
in the Quarto 2 repository.

### Example: a card grid

`card.template`:

```
::: {.custom-card-grid}
$for(items)$
::: {.custom-card}
### [$it.title$]($it.path$)

$if(it.description)$
$it.description$
$endif$
:::

$endfor$
:::
```

Style `.custom-card-grid` and `.custom-card` in your site's CSS.

### Going further

[Listing templates](listing-templates.qmd) covers the rest: the two
rules that fail silently ([links and
images](listing-templates.qmd#links-and-images-must-be-markdown), the
[description
envelope](listing-templates.qmd#descriptions-and-the-placeholder-envelope)),
what each [built-in layout
emits](listing-templates.qmd#what-the-built-in-layouts-emit) so your
template can inherit its styling, and a worked [port of a Quarto 1 EJS
template](listing-templates.qmd#porting-a-quarto-1-ejs-template).

If you are carrying a template over from Quarto 1, start there: Quarto 2
does not run EJS, and a carried-over template warns with
[`Q-12-9`](/errors/listing/Q-12-9.qmd) at the extension and
[`Q-12-24`](/errors/listing/Q-12-24.qmd) at the contents.
